tasks.short: Maintain complete and accurate student records

steps.what: Gather and verify source facts for student records
Enter required student information and maintain record completeness
Resolve gaps and check records against source documents and requirements

tasks.design: Configure required fields, pupil identity selection and duplicate-entry prevention in {OTHER}, the pupil record system. The teacher verifies source facts and resolves missing or conflicting records; no model writes assessments or decides compliance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated entry across local forms makes completeness hard to track.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil record systems already support maintaining pupil information and goal tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether an entry is accurate and which information may be recorded.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve contradictory evidence and record only justified facts.
tasks.altitude: The teacher spends less effort re-entering headers while retaining responsibility for record accuracy.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys offers pupil records and learning-goal tracking.
Required-field configuration may reduce repeated entry; the estimated reduction is unmeasured.

assumptions: In s1 the teacher produces pupil_id, entry_date, record_type, source_reference and verified content from actual observations or authorised documents; all capture and verification time remains in its 45% share. Unresolved identity or content stays pending for manual clarification.
School administration supplies the versioned required-field rules and access permissions; its existing policy work is unchanged, with configuration upkeep counted separately.
Test native fields and duplicate prevention before custom development; no assumed clean feed or automatic interpretation of paper records.
This boundary covers record maintenance, excluding generating reports and making the original pupil assessments.
unknowns: Whether existing record forms already prevent duplicate entry
Which record categories and retention rules the school requires
research_questions: Does a native form remove entry repetition while preserving a verifiable source for each fact?

already_counted.description: Resolve incomplete or conflicting records and inspect saved content

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=45+22.75+20=87.75; gross=12.25%; less 1 focal upkeep gives 11.25% net. Low: current forms already consolidate entry. High: native configuration removes meaningful repeated header entry; collection and checking retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enforce school policies and student rules

steps.what: Establish what happened and identify applicable administration policies and rules
Enforce rules proportionately and explain next steps to students

tasks.design: Keep policy enforcement with the teacher using the school’s current rules in {DOCS}. A searchable rule does not decide what happened or which response is proportionate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Enforcement depends on context and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing policy documents are sufficient; no automation of discipline is proposed.
tasks.human_edge: Listen to pupils and use proportionate responses.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains responsibility for interventions and escalation.

evidence.claim: Applying school rules to individual situations requires contextual teacher judgement.

assumptions: School administration supplies current rules; understanding student accounts stays in s1 and no coded behavior feed is assumed.
Formal incident-record maintenance is a separate task; no reduction is claimed here.
No new system or process is introduced, so additional upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Can teachers locate the current policy during an incident without delaying immediate support?

incremental.description: No new system or process to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=40+60=100. Understanding and intervention are unchanged; no labour savings claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose suitable games, crafts, music and storytelling activities
Arrange materials, spaces and participation for selected activities
Lead activities and adapt support for physical, mental and social development

tasks.design: Use the existing activity library in {DOCS} and preserve the teacher’s organisation and live leadership. The proposed design introduces no generated activity plans because their checking is unlikely to improve this predominantly physical and social work without local evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials, participation and developmental fit are situational.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital activity libraries can support selection, but this answer claims no new time saving.
tasks.still_hard: Include children with different abilities and maintain safe participation.
tasks.human_edge: Adjust the activity when a child is excluded or overwhelmed.
tasks.altitude: The teacher continues selecting, arranging and leading developmental activities.

reach.learn: Recognize barriers and choose suitable adaptations

evidence.claim: Snappet can draft classroom activities, but that capability does not establish reduced material setup or live leadership time.

assumptions: This boundary concerns developmental games, crafts, music and storytelling rather than academic lesson-outline drafting.
The teacher checks available materials and group needs while selecting activities; no structured participation profile is assumed.
Existing resources stay in use and no new upkeep is created.
unknowns: Which participation barriers and materials apply locally
research_questions: Would better indexing of existing activities help selection without adding maintenance work?

incremental.description: No new configuration or generated content to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=15+25+60=100. The design leaves selection, physical preparation and leadership unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare curriculum objectives and course outlines

steps.what: Read curriculum guidelines and identify required objectives for the course
Draft objectives and course outlines against the verified curriculum brief

loop.purpose: Propose a coherent objective sequence within the verified requirements
loop.input: Teacher-produced goal brief, source passages and duration
loop.output: Draft outline with each objective linked to a source requirement
loop.check: Teacher compares each objective and sequence with source meaning, checks coverage, prerequisites and feasible duration; codes alone are insufficient
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; teacher writes disputed objectives manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A prior approved outline is reused first; adapting objectives to a new course requires semantic drafting

steps.what: Approve final objectives and save the course outline for use

tasks.design: Reuse approved outlines in {DOCS} first, then use an approved {LMS} or document assistant for a draft linked to teacher-verified requirements. The teacher checks coverage and educational progression before saving the exact version for use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning curriculum prose into a sequenced outline requires repeated drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Teaching assistants can propose goal-related lesson content; outline generation remains a proposed extension.
tasks.still_hard: Interpret requirements and design a realistic progression for the class.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what deserves emphasis and which prerequisites need attention.

ambition.what: Compare alternate course sequences before selecting one.

tasks.altitude: The teacher gains draft options while keeping final curriculum decisions.

evidence.claim: The Snappet Copilot pilot suggests arithmetic lessons that teachers accept or change.
Source-linked course-outline generation is a proposed adaptation rather than a documented product claim in this digest.

assumptions: In s1 the teacher reads the current source and produces requirement_id, quoted requirement, source_version, course_duration and chosen scope. Its full 25% remains; missing or ambiguous requirements are clarified manually before drafting.
The curriculum owner publishes current source documents; no free structured requirement feed is assumed.
Test reuse and native assistant controls first. No pupil data is required, and the draft cannot publish itself.
unknowns: Which curriculum documents and approved outlines are current
Whether an approved assistant supports source-linked drafting
research_questions: How often do source-linked drafts omit prerequisites or distort curriculum requirements?

already_counted.description: Inspect draft objective meanings and links

incremental.description: Maintain source versions and reusable prompts

approvals.approved_version: Teacher approves exact outline revision and its requirement-source versions before saving for use; any content or source change invalidates approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=25+18+30=73; gross=27%; minus 2 focal upkeep gives 25% net. Low: an existing outline is faster or generated sequences fail review. High: drafting is shorter but source reading and final curriculum judgement remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Record entry and course-outline drafting can become lighter while classroom leadership and pupil decisions remain with the teacher.
reach: Work with administrators on clear record requirements
Compare curriculum coverage with an instructional coordinator
role.ambitious_version: Use preparation capacity to consider better course sequences without automating discipline or developmental interaction.
